title: Objection and Q&A bank with sourced claims
story: As the candidate I need a rehearsed bank of the questions a skeptical CTO and an AI champion will ask, with crisp answers, depth if pushed and sourced facts, so that I answer honestly and briefly under pressure and keep the 40 minutes on track.
acceptance: strategy/objection-handling.md has exactly 8 group headings "## 1." to "## 8." in this order: security and data; compliance and regulation; quality and risk of AI-written code; productivity evidence; cost; competition and 'we already have Copilot'; change management and skills; vendor and concentration risk. grep -c '^## [1-8]\. ' strategy/objection-handling.md prints 8.

At least 25 objections and at least 3 per group, each a "### O-nn." heading holding the objection in the asker's own words (CTO or champion): grep -c '^### O-' strategy/objection-handling.md prints 25 or more. Each objection has the lines "- **Asker:**", "- **Answer:**", "- **If pushed:**" (followed by 3 to 6 indented sub-bullets), "- **Claims:**" and "- **Bridge:**"; for each label  grep -c '^- \*\*<label>:\*\*' strategy/objection-handling.md  equals the objection count.

Answers are crisp and sayable: node -e 'const t=require("fs").readFileSync("strategy/objection-handling.md","utf8");const a=[...t.matchAll(/^- \*\*Answer:\*\* (.+)$/gm)].map(m=>m[1].trim().split(/\s+/).length);console.log(a.length,Math.max(...a))'  prints the objection count and a maximum of 65 or less (about 28 seconds at 140 wpm). Each Answer is 2 to 3 sentences, executive line first, conceding what is true before reframing. Each "If pushed" gives engineer-level depth and names where more lives (leave-behind or backup slide by deliverable id: D5, D6, D7 or D10).

The top of the file has a three-line summary, an index table of every objection (id, short form, group, asker) so it can be scanned live, and a "Top 8 to rehearse" list ranked by how much a wrong answer would hurt the meeting.

Honesty rules (ADR-006): productivity answers acknowledge mixed evidence, then point to measuring on FinTechCo's own work; no superlative without a named, dated source; no disparagement of any competitor; the Copilot objection is framed as "if we already license an IDE assistant" and never asserts FinTechCo owns any product (facts.json: no agentic tools today, evaluating several); compliance answers say what controls Claude Code provides and that FinTechCo's compliance team decides fit, never "Claude Code is compliant".

Every external fact carries a [CLM-6xx] id that exists in the shard with status verified or partial, or a specific [CLM-?: ...] placeholder. Every objection in groups 1 and 2, and any other touching data handling, retention, training, certifications, deployment boundaries or regulatory fit, carries the line "- **Trust-review:** required" (ADR-003 section 4.2): grep -c 'Trust-review' strategy/objection-handling.md prints 8 or more.

research/claims/strategy.json validates against org/contracts/claims.schema.json with ids only in CLM-600..CLM-649: node -e 'const c=require("./research/claims/strategy.json");console.log(c.length,c.every(x=>/^CLM-6[0-4][0-9]$/.test(x.id)))'  prints a count of 12 or more and true. Every claim has at least one official source (title, url, publisher, date if shown), accessed 2026-10-xx, a safeWording when partial or refuted, and usedIn listing strategy/objection-handling.md.

The shard covers at least: data handling, retention and training on commercial inputs; the permission model and sandboxing; managed settings and policy enforcement; hooks, audit logging or OpenTelemetry monitoring; deployment through Amazon Bedrock and Google Cloud Vertex AI; certifications exactly as listed on Anthropic's Trust Center; and productivity evidence including at least one result that found a slowdown and one that found a speedup. Anything not verifiable is recorded as unverified with notes and appears in the document only as a placeholder.

node org/contracts/validate.mjs passes for this ticket's files: no FAIL line names research/claims/strategy.json or strategy/objection-handling.md (failures naming other teams' files are out of scope).
Only this ticket's two paths were changed; no secrets, Anthropic brand assets, invented customer names, quotes or numbers; a handoff listing remaining placeholders is posted to hub strategy.
brief:
Audience: the candidate rehearsing, then answering live inside a 40-minute meeting, so every Answer must be sayable in about 25 seconds (65 words max at ~140 wpm). The CTO is blunt, security-first, 20+ years in financial services IT, skeptical without proven enterprise adoption. The Head of Digital Transformation needs lines to reuse with colleagues.

Step 1, source first: shard research/claims/strategy.json, ids CLM-600..649 only (claims.schema.json). Official documentation first (ADR-006 hierarchy): Claude Code docs at code.claude.com/docs (security, data usage, permissions, settings and managed settings, hooks, sandboxing, monitoring-usage, Amazon Bedrock, Google Vertex AI), the Anthropic Trust Center and commercial terms, AWS and Google Cloud docs for hosted-model data handling. For productivity use original sources only; candidates to look up are METR's randomized trial with experienced open-source developers, DORA's AI-assisted development research, large company field experiments and Anthropic's own published research. Check each; never use numbers from memory. Write each claim as it may be said aloud; use partial plus safeWording when a source says less than you want. Aim for 12 to 25 claims. Load WebSearch and WebFetch with ToolSearch query "select:WebSearch,WebFetch".

Step 2, write the bank in the format of the acceptance criteria. Per objection: Asker; Answer (concede what is true, then reframe); If pushed (depth); Claims; Trust-review tag where it applies; Bridge (one line back to an ADR-005 ask: security review, pilot cohort, metrics owner, kickoff date).

Cover at least: code leaving our perimeter; training on our data; prompt injection and exfiltration; secrets and card data in repos; audit trail and evidence for auditors (SOX, PCI DSS, GLBA and model risk guidance appear as placeholders only, never quoted from memory); accountability for AI-written changes; hallucinated dependencies and subtle bugs; mixed productivity studies; "show me the ROI"; unpredictable token spend; the incumbent IDE assistant and other agents under evaluation; senior-engineer pushback and junior skill atrophy; single-vendor and model-availability risk, exit and portability (Bedrock and Vertex as deployment choices).

Pitfalls: never promise a productivity number; never say Claude Code makes FinTechCo compliant; placeholders must say exactly what to source.
